subject: MedOrbit Health — Vendor Security Questionnaire + evidence requests (Redwood Inference)
body:
From: Lena Cho <lena.cho@medorbithealth.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: vendorrisk@medorbithealth.com, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@medorbithealth.com>
Date: Sun, Feb 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: MedOrbit Health — Vendor Security Questionnaire + evidence requests (Redwood Inference)

Hi Dr. Rahman,

Following our call last week, attached are:
1) Our Vendor Security Questionnaire (v3)
2) Evidence request list (standard for PHI vendors)

A few items we want to confirm up front (to avoid back-and-forth):
- Whether Redwood stores or retains prompts/outputs by default, and if we can contractually require no retention.
- Audit logging: what events are captured, retention options, and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM.
- Encryption/KMS: do you support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) for Private/VPC?
- Subprocessors and where data is processed (regions).

If you can return the questionnaire by EOW, we can keep our review on track.

Thank you,
Lena Cho
Vendor Risk Analyst
MedOrbit Health

Attachments:
- MedOrbit_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx
- MedOrbit_Security_Evidence_Request_List.pdf


---

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Cho <lena.cho@medorbithealth.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@medorbithealth.com>, vendorrisk@medorbithealth.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Feb 1, 2026 at 12:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: MedOrbit Health — Vendor Security Questionnaire + evidence requests (Redwood Inference)

Hi Lena (and Sanjay),

Thanks — received.

Quick note on evidence: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and most detailed control narratives under NDA. If you already have a MedOrbit NDA template, feel free to send it over; otherwise we can provide ours.

Initial answers on the items you called out:

1) Prompt/output retention
- In Redwood Hosted API: we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models. Operational metadata is collected for service delivery (e.g., request/response timing, error codes).
- For content retention, our posture is “minimum necessary” and configurable based on deployment and settings. For regulated workloads, we typically recommend Dedicated or Private deployments to meet stricter data-handling requirements.
- In Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem style): customer traffic stays within the customer-controlled network boundary. Audit/log export can be configured to customer systems.

2) Audit logging
- We support audit logging for administrative actions (e.g., auth/RBAC changes, key config changes, deployment/rollout actions) and platform events.
- Export options can include delivery to customer-controlled storage/log systems depending on deployment (Private/Dedicated) and region.

3) Encryption / customer-managed keys
- We support encryption in transit and at rest.
- For Private deployments, we support integration points for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integrations vary by environment; we can confirm specifics based on your target cloud and architecture).

4) Subprocessors / regions
- We can provide a current subprocessor list and region availability. For Private, the customer controls where the system runs.

To accelerate, I’ve attached our Healthcare Security FAQ addendum (high-level, questionnaire-friendly language). Marcus (Security Eng) and Olga (GRC) are CC’d and will help with the evidence packet + questionnaire completion.

A couple questions from our side:
- Are you evaluating Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private/VPC as the intended steady-state for PHI workloads?
- Do you require a BAA at this stage, or after technical evaluation?

Best,
Aisha

Dr. Aisha Rahman
CISO, Redwood Inference

Attachment:
- Redwood_ABM_Healthcare_Security_FAQ_Addendum.pdf

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@medorbithealth.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lena Cho <lena.cho@medorbithealth.com>, vendorrisk@medorbithealth.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 8:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: MedOrbit Health — Vendor Security Questionnaire + evidence requests (Redwood Inference)

Hi Aisha,

Helpful, thank you.

Our intended steady-state is Private/VPC (AWS) for anything that touches PHI. We may use Hosted for non-PHI dev/testing, but we want the security review to be anchored around the Private deployment.

A few clarifications we’ll need for the questionnaire:

1) Audit logs
- Do audit logs include model invocation events (who/what/when), or only admin/control plane actions?
- Can we set retention to 1 year and export to Splunk (HEC) or S3?

2) Retention
- Can you confirm: prompts/outputs are not stored by default in Private?
- If any operational logs contain request bodies, can that be disabled?

3) Evidence
- We’ll need SOC 2 Type II, most recent penetration test summary, incident response policy, and subprocessor list.

We can route an NDA today. Is there a preferred signatory on your side?

Regards,
Sanjay Patel
Director of Security
MedOrbit Health


---

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@medorbithealth.com>
Cc: Lena Cho <lena.cho@medorbithealth.com>, vendorrisk@medorbithealth.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 10:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: MedOrbit Health — Vendor Security Questionnaire + evidence requests (Redwood Inference)

Hi Sanjay,

Understood — anchoring on Private/VPC is the right approach for this review.

On your questions:

1) Audit logs
- Scope: In Private deployments, we focus audit logging on administrative/control plane actions and security-relevant platform events (access/auth changes, configuration changes, deployment actions, key configuration updates, etc.).
- Model invocation events: We can capture request-level operational telemetry (timing/error metrics) without retaining prompt/output bodies. Where teams need additional application-layer logging, we generally recommend that be implemented in the customer environment (upstream of Redwood) so PHI handling stays fully under your controls.
- Export: Yes, we can support export to customer-controlled destinations (commonly S3 or SIEM pipelines) in Private, subject to final architecture. Retention is typically governed by where you store the exported logs (e.g., your S3/Splunk retention policy) rather than Redwood retaining them long-term.

2) Retention
- Private/VPC: prompts/outputs are not retained by Redwood by default. We can also disable any settings that would log request bodies.
- Operational logs: standard operational logs are designed to avoid request/response bodies; we capture metadata needed for reliability and troubleshooting (timestamps, latency, status/error codes, request identifiers).

3) Evidence
- SOC 2 Type II: available under NDA.
- Pen test summary: available under NDA.
- IR policy + subprocessor list: shareable (some sections may still be gated under NDA depending on detail level).

NDA signatory: you can send to me, and I’ll route internally the same day.

Best,
Aisha

Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 3:27 PM PST
Subject: Re: MedOrbit Health — Vendor Security Questionnaire + evidence requests (Redwood Inference)

Hi Lena,

Jumping in from Redwood GRC.

We’ve started filling out the MedOrbit questionnaire and have two items where your intended architecture impacts the response:

1) Identity / SSO for Private
- Do you require SAML SSO for admin console access during the evaluation, or is it acceptable to use named accounts with enforced MFA initially?

2) Log export format
- For Splunk, are you expecting HEC directly from the Redwood environment, or is “export to S3 + your forwarder” acceptable?

Once we have these, we’ll finalize the remaining sections and align the evidence packet for release under NDA.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
GRC Lead
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: MedOrbit Health — Vendor Security Questionnaire + evidence requests (Redwood Inference)

Hi Olga,

1) SSO: For eval, named accounts + enforced MFA is acceptable. Before production PHI, we’ll require SAML SSO + RBAC.

2) Export: “Export to S3 + our forwarder” is acceptable. We’ll note Splunk HEC as preferred but not required.

Also sharing our NDA template in a separate email to Aisha for signature.

Thank you,
Lena
